selections.comment: D DAY MAJOR WINTER appeals most after proving he can last beyond a mile with a resectable second-placed finish over an extended 1m3f at Lingfield 11 days ago. This slightly shorter trip could prove to be ideal given the way that race panned out and he won't need much of a step forward to assert his authority under top-weight. Leicester runner-up Shabu Shabu is feared most, although Buck Barrow also has strong possibilities at this level.

selections.comment: Nivelle's Magic was back on a previous winning mark when scoring over 1m4f at Southwell on her most recent start, but she has a 5lb higher rating, a 53-day absence to overcome and two additional furlongs to cope with here. Those factors are persuasive enough to suggest looking elsewhere, with BLENHEIM LAD forwarded as the first one to consider. Already a winner over this distance, that proven stamina earns the Camilla Poulton-trained gelding the vote. Adrian and Jimmy Mark can also feature.

selections.comment: This could be well within the reach of MAGNETITE, who won't need much of a step forward to get off the mark. The Wathnan Racing-owned colt was a respectable third behind a much better-fancied stable companion on his seasonal debut at Chepstow last month and should be spot on for a bolder showing in this, his qualifying run for a handicap mark. Outlandish, Pantani and Mum's Angel are other unexposed options to consider.

selections.comment: This looks open with the likes of handicap debutants Maybe Not, Amica and Key Witness all seemingly capable of better, but it is HUNKY DORY that gets the vote. The son of Pinatubo was perhaps in need of the outing at Newmarket at the beginning of last month, though he took a marked leap forward to finish an extremely creditable fifth in a warm York contest latest. Eased 1lb in the handicap, it would come as no great surprise were he to find further progress and land the spoils.

That said, it might be worth taking a chance on SCENARIO. The low-mileage three-year-old posted a solid effort when fourth at Brighton earlier this month. Cheekpieces are applied for the first time and they could elicit some improvement. Irish raider Yquem makes her handicap bow and the booking of David Egan is noteworthy.

selections.comment: THREE YORKSHIREMEN was able to take advantage of a sliding handicap mark when on target over 1m3f at Kempton recently. Cornish Storm has been in solid form under both codes and must feature prominently in calculations, while Run Of Luck appeals most of the remaining trio.

Huit Reflets goes well here and can make sure the selection is kept up to his work, while National Question is another C&D winner that cannot be ruled out having returned from a break/wind surgery with a fourth-placed finish on the Flat at Pontefract last month.

selections.comment: BENY NAHAR ROAD is readily nominated after he won in a cosy manner at Southwell 19 days ago. A 6lb higher rating looks fair and the six-year-old's case is boosted as he already boasts some C&D experience. Glory And Honour's recent second-placed finish over hurdles here should have kept him ticking over nicely and he rates a key player in what is likely to be a tactical affair. Scots Poet can utilise his course knowledge to out manoeuvre Disco Annie for third place.

selections.comment: Fortune The Brave's latest start is best forgotten as he unseated at the first flight at Punchestown. The Irish raider has to be of interest in taking this potentially winnable race. However, he has to concede plenty of weight to the hat-trick seeking MAN OF ACTION, who won over this C&D in early-May before following up at Perth a fortnight ago. A 5lb higher rating might not be enough to prevent him from extending the winning sequence, while Foxwood and Brave Adam are the pick of the rest.

selections.comment: This isn't the deepest of contests and it could provide MAGGIES BOY the perfect opportunity in which to break his hurdling duck. Jennie Candlish's gelding has posted a number of solid efforts in defeat and the addition of a first-time tongue-tie could eke out a little more. Moonbow was a well-held third at Perth a fortnight ago but he ought to have learnt plenty from that experience and is one of the likelier candidates. Mayor Kingston is a half-brother to a multiple hurdles winner and market support would be noteworthy.

Royal Deeside was also victorious over track and trip last time so he merits the utmost respect, as does Fontwell scorer Fortunate Fella. O'Faolains Glory is no back number either.

selections.comment: FEACH AMACH hasn't looked back since undergoing wind surgery in March, winning three of her four starts since - the most recent of those coming at Kelso last month. Adam Nicol's mare is 4lb higher today and would require a career-best but, while some of these have a bit to prove, she ought to go very close. A drop in trip and a return to this venue could hold the key to Les's Legacy, who merits respect along with handicap debutant Kow Boy Sivola.

Tim Easterby's filly sets a good standard dropping in class and her experience could prove crucial. 300,000-pound newcomer Enchant must be monitored in the betting, along with American Flight, a half-sister to the Group-placed Les Bleus.

selections.comment: KARMOLOGY has been the bridesmaid on three previous occasions in Listed races but is a game mare who could step up here. The Karl Burke-trained five-year-old is set to encounter ideal ground conditions and, still unexposed over the trip, there is plenty to like about her. Ralph Beckett has a good record in this and plays another strong hand, with the less-exposed Meribella shading preference over Allonsy as the main danger. Santorini Star could go well too.

selections.comment: SURREY FIRE is open to progression and given that his dam won the Cesarewitch during her career, there are very good reasons to expect the Hughie Morrison-trained four-year-old will have the stamina reserves to have a big impact. This is no easy task and the likes of Almudena and Diamand De Vindecy, a C&D winner in April, will keep the selection honest. Captain Potter could also be a surprise package in an open race.

selections.comment: NIVELLE'S MAGIC was back to form last time winning comfortably when eased close home at Southwell, she's already won at the track and could back that impressive win up here. Jimmy Mark won at Bath three starts back despite not getting a clear run at Chepstow, he's backed that up with second places since and latest was travelling best before hanging badly at Windsor last time, he looks the main danger. Beggarman was below par last time at Chepstow but showed better form last term over 1m6f, so the return to this trip from 5lb below his last winning mark should see improvement.

selections.comment: ARCTIC DAWN has been running well in decent handicaps this term, unlucky last time when not much went right but fourth to Mum's Tipple, can get off the mark at the 9th time of asking. Magnetite can run him close, he was well backed last time in a novice at Chepstow, improving from his debut run in behind some decent opposition. Pantani improved up in trip on quicker conditions last time when third at Leicester, there may be more improvement in him. Merapi is an interesting debutant, she is well-bred and has 5lb weight allowance so is one to keep an eye on.

selections.comment: KEY WITNESS was given a nice ride and showed a willing attitude to make all and win at Chelsmford last time out, he makes his turf debut here and with form franked several times from that effort (including third and seventh winning since) he will be tough to beat if proving as effective on turf from an opening mark of 72. selections.comment: An open race where a host of the field can be given chances but it is maiden LOVE TRUE who appeals most. She travelled powerfully in a strong novice last time and though her finishing effort was lacking once again she looks well treated back in a handicap with her previous winter handicap form franked. Last year's winner Malangen is feared most from an 8lb lower mark as he caught the eye last time travelling powerfully before his stamina gave way over 3m. Another veteran who is slipping down the weights is Allbetsoff and he can't be dismissed given his fine record here.

selections.comment: A tight contest where none of the quartet can be ruled out. There is the potential for an easy lead for DISCO ANNIE here though with all of her opponents being strong stayers who liked to be played late. She was given too much to do herself last time at a sharp track when well backed but still ran well and is well treated on her hurdles form. If allowed her own way in front she will be tough to peg back here. The progressive Beny Nahar Road looks the biggest threat if getting a decent test as he was a cosy winner last time and has finally got his jumping together. Veteran Glory And Honour holds little in secret from the handicapper but will be running on at the finish and isn't totally ruled out either.

selections.comment: C&D winner Man Of Action is likely to prove popular in his hat trick bid and with some justification given the willing attitude he showed to get up last time but he will need a stiff test to continue his progress so could be vulnerable to a pair bringing in strong Irish form. FORTUNE THE BRAVE was well fancied for his handicap debut but failed to complete and looks worth another chance judged on his decent maiden form at up to 3m. The British handicapper has given him every chance and with the drying ground in his favour he is worth chancing. Brave Adam was too bad to be true last time but is thrown in on his Irish chase form and is also worth a market check ahead of his stable debut in first time cheekpieces.

selections.comment: A weak maiden which can go to point and bumper winner MOONBOW. He was green and let down by his jumping on hurdle debut but still manage to place proving his stamina for this far and a repeat of that will make him tough to beat. Maggies Boy has had plenty of chances now proving frustrating but he had at least shown a consistent level of form until his latest outing so is fancied to fill the runner up spot. Yapper Hill showed minor promise in points and may do best of the rest on his hurdle debut.

selections.comment: This looks a match race between last time out C&D winners ROYAL DEESIDE and Marty McFly.The latter has seen the form of that victory boosted by a placed horse since so is strongly respected but the former impressed immensely with his jumping last time so is taken to follow up. He's only been raised 4lb, is open to further progress in this sphere and remains on a good mark judged on his hurdle and flat form. Of the others veteran Cracking Destiny is fancied to fill the places off this much reduced mark. He has enthusiasm and strike rate concerns but should be competitive off this rating.

selections.comment: The progressive Feach Amach likely to be well fancied having won 3 of her last 4 but she was a fortunate winner last time as a rival went wrong late and she may struggle to follow up off this revised mark. The unexposed KOW BOY SIVOLA is picked instead having returned to his best form when midfield here last time despite racing freely. He looks to have been let in lightly by the handicapper and should appreciate the longer trip. The most interesting rival is undoubtedly Coventry who found 2m too sharp last time but is dangerously well treated on his Irish form and he did prove he retained most of his ability in the autumn.

Bleep Test brings solid experience and consistent form to the the table in this small field, and is a key player if running to the same form as her other three starts. American Flight also boasts quality pedigree as 230,000gns Starpangledbanner filly, but the others are preferred.

He drops in class and rates the pick to returning to winning ways here. Creatif has been in excellent heart since a wind op, scoring on Newcastle first start back and going close last twice, so looks a contender. Expert Witness was somewhat below form on her latest start, but won well at Windsor prior and could bounce back.

selections.comment: CINNODIN returns to the turf after a consistent all-weather spell and looks like the one to beat in this close contest, having won nicely over two miles at Kempton three starts back. Captain Potter is a solid and reliable type who close here last time and should be in the mix over this slightly longer trip. Surrey Fire is unexposed over this distance and, with Tom Marquand notably booked, rates a potential threat if settling better than she has previously.

selections.comment: PARTISAN HERO has been flying this year and showed real determination when getting back to winning ways by a head over 7f at Epsom last time. He drops in trip again but remains capable of going well again with the booking of Rossa Ryan a plus. Rare Change had excuses when well held last time but was in strong form beforehand with wins at Windsor and York. Fast ground and return to 6f should suit. Native Instinct remains lightly raced and could still have improvement in him based on last year's three starts.

Mount King is a course winner who wasn't disgraced last time and remains a value selection at the right price if repeating his penultimate start. Style Of Life got back on track at Chester and could be dangerous if allowed to dictate, though firmer ground may not play to strengths.

races.verdict: ADORLA OF ACHILL took a big step forward when getting off the mark on her second handicap start at Haydock and, with Rossa Ryan now in the saddle, she's taken to follow up in more than capable hands. Mount King is a course winner who wasn't disgraced last time and remains a value selection at the right price if repeating his penultimate start.
